name: reviewer-dev-via-test decide(approved) → coordinator final wake-up
description:
ADR-044 Slice 4 chain terminal. Fires when CBG (reviewer-dev-via-test) decides approved — the integration test passed and the diff is sane. Spawns a final coordinator loop with the CBG loop_id so the coordinator can read_loop_result and synthesize a user-facing reply via decide(action=respond_direct). The existing coordinator/03b-respond-direct.json rule then publishes the reply on the user-response bus.

Mirrors autoresearch rule 08-reviewer-approved-to-coordinator shape: same wake-up pattern, scoped to the dev-via-test pack's CBG role + approved token.

on_enter.subject: agent.task.coordinator
on_enter.prompt:
The dev-via-test chain you dispatched has reached its terminal. CBG (reviewer-dev-via-test) at loop $entity.instance ran the integration test command across the full task scope and APPROVED the work.

Your job now is to deliver the result to the user. You are not classifying, delegating, or re-reviewing — the chain has already done the work and CBG has validated it.

Iteration 1 — call read_loop_result(loop_id=$entity.instance) to read CBG's approved verdict. CBG's reason summarises: what shipped (the user-facing capability), integration test result, any noteworthy observations from the diff.

Iteration 2 — call decide(action="respond_direct", reason="<your synthesised user-facing answer>"). The respond_direct rule publishes your reason on the user-response bus.

Write the reason as plain prose addressing the user directly. The user asked for an implementation; tell them what shipped, that the acceptance test passed, and any caveats worth flagging (e.g., if some tasks were marked blocked by Ralph but the integration test still passed because other tasks covered the scope). 3-6 sentences is usually right; don't dump CBG's full rollup, pick the headline.
